Dana: Thanks for jumping on, Luis. Walk me through a normal week at Bayline.
Luis: Sure. Bayline Pest Solutions, we're in Charlotte, 14 techs on routes, mostly restaurants, a few dental offices, and two big hospital accounts.
Dana: Where does your time actually go?
Luis: Estimates. After every inspection I'm up late writing the estimate at the kitchen table. Square footage, bait stations, frequency, the price. That's about five hours a week, and I keep reusing the last estimate and leaving the old client's name in it.
Dana: What else?
Luis: Sick calls. A tech calls out sick by text at 6 a.m. and I'm on the route board figuring out who can pick up their stops and who's already near overtime. It's an hour a day, easy.
Dana: Where does the schedule live?
Luis: Routes are in PestPac. Chemical inventory is an Excel file Rhonda keeps. Billing is QuickBooks Online.
Dana: How do customers reach you?
Luis: Email, mostly. Kitchen managers send me "we saw activity by the dish pit again" and I have to log it, tell the route lead, and make sure someone goes back.
Luis: Every Monday I'm supposed to send each account a service summary — what we treated, trap counts, anything we found. I spend two hours every Monday on that when I actually do it.
Dana: And getting paid?
Luis: Past-due invoices. About $14,000 over sixty days right now. Chasing that is three or four hours a week.
Dana: If you woke up tomorrow and one thing was done, what would it be?
Luis: The Monday service summaries, done and waiting for me to approve. Plus a list of which accounts had activity complaints last week.
Dana: Any hard rules? Things it should never do?
Luis: Two. Never quote a price to a customer without my sign-off. And never call or email anyone at St. Mary's Hospital except Dr. Okafor's office manager, Pam.
Dana: Tone?
Luis: Friendly, short, no jargon.
